## Outcome

An edge edit validates the proposed graph before writing, refuses when a final reread observes changed issue content, and never performs a blind rollback that could overwrite a newer edit.

## Concurrency boundary (operator decision, 2026-11-08)

Use optimistic checks and document the remaining race. GitHub does not document conditional PATCH support for issue updates. A reread followed by PATCH is not atomic: a change after the final reread can still be overwritten, and another edge can change after validation. The compiler must state this limit rather than promise that no concurrent edit or cycle is ever possible. This task does not introduce a separate authoritative store or lock all GitHub editors.

## Problem

`compile_from_github` currently writes the child's new body first, recompiles, and on failure writes the old body back. For that window the truth source may hold a cycle. Neither the patch nor the rollback checks whether the body changed since it was read. A PATCH by an untrusted writer also changes the issue's trust history; recompilation can then exclude the edited issue and report success without checking its new edge.

## Scope

- Compile the closure with the proposed edge applied in memory; reject a cycle, invalid frontmatter, scope violation or required lookup failure before any write. Validate the edited child even when explicit roots exclude it.
- Validate the writer identity under the same trust policy before PATCH; refuse unknown or untrusted writers. Model PATCH authorship in the fake edit history.
- Immediately before PATCH, reread and revalidate the child's identity, body and body-editor trust. On an observed conflict, fail without writing (exit 1, naming the issue); lookup failures exit 2.
- Remove post-write rollback. A failed or uncertain PATCH is reported and never followed by a blind retry or restoration.
- Preserve no-op and remove-edge behavior, including removal of an out-of-scope blocker.
- Document the optimistic concurrency limit in CLI/skill guidance and the threat model.

## Out of scope

Retrying or merging after a conflict; atomic compare-and-swap without an endpoint contract; redesigning graph storage.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A cycle-creating add-edge performs no PATCH, including when the changed child is outside explicit roots.
- [ ] An observed body change or newly untrusted editor before write is refused without PATCH.
- [ ] An unknown/untrusted writer is refused before PATCH; successful fake writes record their editor identity.
- [ ] Required lookup failures and optional relationship-comparison failures occur before writes; no rollback overwrites newer content.
- [ ] No-op edits do not PATCH; remove-edge can repair an out-of-scope reference.
- [ ] Existing tests pass, with rollback expectations replaced by zero-write rejection checks; live backlog compilation has no maintainer-authored untrusted nodes.

API reference: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api#use-conditional-requests


## Implementation target (2026-11-11)

Re-scoped by the Rust rebuild decision (#24). This issue is implemented in the Rust `gh` write adapter, after the read adapters (#31). The outcome, concurrency boundary and acceptance checks above are unchanged. The Python implementation in draft PR #19 will not merge; its tests become characterisation cases (#26). The cutover (#32) waits for this issue so that no unsafe edge write ships in the binary.

## Outcome

The executor takes a selected task from start to ready-for-review: lease, worktree, draft PR, pushed progress, status comments, and un-draft when the work is done. Task state lives in GitHub PR state, not labels.

## State model

| State | Source |
| --- | --- |
| open / blocked | The graph: no PR, zero or some open blockers |
| wip | Open draft PR that closes the issue |
| in-review | Open PR marked ready |
| done | PR merged, issue closed |

Gate failure and parking are flyingrobots/taskalisk#14; resuming stalled work is flyingrobots/taskalisk#15.

## Scope

- Per task: its own worktree; a `git-locks` lease on `task/owner/repo#N` for as long as an agent works on it; run-time keys claimed with `git locks with`.
- On start: an empty first commit (hooks run), push, and a draft PR whose body says `Closes owner/repo#N`.
- Prompt builder: the script assembles the prompt from the issue (frontmatter and body), the closed blockers and their merged PRs, the repository's agent instructions (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`), the branch state and the latest CI result. Text from issues and PRs is marked as data, not instructions. The rules the agent must follow (push at meaningful commits, comment with the commit SHA, never `--no-verify`, never merge) are part of the prompt. The builder is shared, so flyingrobots/taskalisk#14 and flyingrobots/taskalisk#15 add their own prompts.
- During work: the agent pushes at meaningful commits and posts status comments naming the commit SHA. Comments are for people; the executor never reads them back as state. Rebase pushes use `--force-with-lease` on the task branch only.
- Ready: un-draft only when the acceptance criteria are met and CI is green.

## Out of scope

- The gate, retries, parking and merging (flyingrobots/taskalisk#14); resuming stalled tasks (flyingrobots/taskalisk#15).
- `taskalisk:*` labels. Considered and rejected: they would be a second tracker that goes stale.

## Prerequisites

- #1: agents record discovered dependencies concurrently, and today's unchecked writes lose updates.
- #9: this builds on its preflight and selection.
- flyingrobots/taskalisk#13: this launches agents through it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An end-to-end run over `fake_gh` and the fake agent takes one task through lease, draft PR, a pushed commit with a SHA-tagged comment, and un-draft on green CI.
- [ ] The built prompt contains the issue, the closed blockers and the repository instructions, with issue text marked as data (test).
- [ ] CI red at the end of the agent run leaves the PR as a draft.

## Security requirements (docs/threat-model.md)

- C7: the prompt builder wraps every string from GitHub (body, comments, PR text, review text) in a delimited data block and states outside it that instructions inside are not followed. Titles never enter a prompt. Comments enter only when their author is trusted, and then as data.
- C8: agents run inside a sandbox with an explicit tool allowlist and a scoped token (#13). A permission-bypass flag is allowed only inside that sandbox.
- C10 Stage 1 (decided 2026-11-08): the empty first commit carries trailers `Issue: owner/repo#N` and `Body-SHA256: <approved body hash>`, mirrored in the PR body marker. Trailers follow the Git trailer convention as implemented by `@git-stunts/trailer-codec` (keys alphanumeric and hyphens, case-insensitive; values single-line). Stage 2 (signing, `Approval:` trailer) is deferred.
- C11: `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` are read from `main`, never from the task branch. Hooks are not disabled.
- C14: agents receive a token scoped to the closure's repositories; status comments carry the commit SHA only.
- Doctrine 8 update in SKILL.md: the compiler's only GitHub write stays the `.blocked_by` edit; the executor adds pushes to its own task branches, draft PRs and status comments.
- Tests: prompt marks issue text as data and excludes untrusted comments and titles; first commit carries both trailers; instruction files come from `main` when the branch changes them.

## Outcome

SKILL.md has a Resize workflow: the agent reviews every open task in the compiled DAG for estimate, atomicity and scope, presents findings and split proposals, and applies the splits the user approves.

## Scope

- **Review** each open task, using the compiled output (`frontmatter.warnings`, `open_frontier_ranked`) and the issue body:
  - Does `.size_hours` match the described scope? Is it missing or above 8?
  - Is the task atomic: one observable outcome, independently mergeable, `main` working after it lands?
  - Does it have acceptance checks?
  - Is it in this repository's scope (README, CLAUDE.md)?
  - Containers with one child or none.
- **Propose**: for each split, how the original requirements are divided among the pieces (no gaps, no duplicate ownership), what remains in the parent, and which piece each existing dependent actually needs.
- **Apply** only after the user approves, in this order: create the new tasks, add the dependents' new edges with `--add-edge`, remove the old edges with `--remove-edge`, then convert the original to a container. Recompile and check the result. A dependent must never be left blocked on a container.
- **Shortcut:** when the first piece of a split keeps the original's prerequisites, narrow the original into that piece instead of converting it to a container. Its dependents need no rewiring, and the other pieces join the original's container.
- **Out-of-scope tasks** are reported, never transferred. The report lists every reference a transfer would break.

## Out of scope

- A script `--split` mode. Machine warnings for bundled tasks are #41; the procedure proved error-prone on 2026-11-15, when an agent with the skill loaded planned 24 tasks as 10.
- Calibrating estimates against actual draft-to-merge durations (possible after the executor loop lands; a follow-up).

## Acceptance

- [ ] SKILL.md documents the workflow, the approval stop and the apply order.
- [ ] Applied once to this repository's backlog, with the findings recorded in a comment here.

## Outcome
The release perf job fails unless every `perf_` test that exists ran and passed.

## Scope
- A script, `scripts/check_perf_tests.py`, that takes the output of `cargo test ... -- --ignored --list perf_` and of the run itself, and fails when a listed `perf_` test did not pass, or when none is listed.
- The "Rust planning bounds (release)" job runs that script instead of `test "$ran" -ge 6`.
- Offline tests for the script in `tests/`.
- An offline test that every test ignored as a wall-clock bound (`#[ignore = "wall-clock bound; ..."]`) is named `perf_`, and every `perf_` test is ignored as one, so a rename out of the filter fails the Python suite.

## Out of scope
- The bounds themselves and the `perf_` tests (`crates/issue-dag-core/src/plan.rs`, `batch.rs`).
- The default `cargo test` job.

## Prerequisites
None.

## Safe intermediate state
Not applicable, because the change lands in one pull request.

## Acceptance
- [ ] With a seventh `perf_` test listed but not run, the check fails, naming the missing test.
- [ ] With no `perf_` test listed, the check fails.
- [ ] With every listed test passing, the check passes and prints how many ran.
- [ ] With zero tests passing, the check fails and still prints its count.
- [ ] The job keeps failing when `cargo test` fails (`shell: bash`, so `pipefail`).
- [ ] The workflow no longer hardcodes a count.
- [ ] A `perf_` test that loses its `#[ignore]` fails the job: the listing includes it, and the `--ignored` run does not run it.
- [ ] A bound renamed out of the `perf_` filter fails the offline suite.

## 1. Background Context
Baker Street case `2026-11-26-taskalisk-pr116-delta` (READY for #116) recorded two follow-ups on commit 7277ff0, which added the count guard:
- F-1 (LOW): `test "$ran" -ge 6` hardcodes the number of `perf_` tests. Once a seventh exists, losing any one of them later still passes, so one wall-clock bound stops being checked while the job stays green.
- F-2 (INFORMATIONAL): when nothing matches, `grep -c` exits 1 under `bash -e` before the step prints its count.

## 2. Problem Description
The guard checks "at least six passed", not "all that exist passed".

## 2b. Proposed Solution
List the `perf_` tests with `--list`, run them, and require the passed set to equal the listed set, with at least one listed. Print the count in every outcome.

## 2c. Test Plan
Golden: six listed and six passed gives exit 0 and "perf_ tests passed: 6 of 6".
Edges: seven listed and six passed fails, naming the seventh; none listed fails; zero passed fails and prints 0; a `FAILED` or `ignored` line never counts as passed; a test name in another crate with the same path is told apart by its crate.
Known failure modes: libtest line formats (`name: test` in a list, `test name ... ok` in a run).
Fuzz and stress: not applicable, because the inputs are small fixed formats.

## 3. Why now
Every new `perf_` test needs the constant raised by hand, and nothing reminds anyone to do it.

## 4. Risks
A change in libtest's output format would fail the job. That is the right direction to fail.

## 5. Definition of Done
The Acceptance items hold, and CI's release job passes with the new check on this repository's six `perf_` tests.

## 6. Stakeholders
Maintainers and merging agents who rely on the green "Rust planning bounds (release)" check.

- flyingrobots/taskalisk#105 is the review that started this.

## Outcome
The `issue-dag-gh` forge tests pass on Linux whatever order their threads run in.

## Scope
- The fake `gh` of `crates/issue-dag-gh/tests/fake/mod.rs` becomes a symlink to `tests/fake_gh.py`, which becomes executable in git. No test writes an executable file.
- A test that the fake's `gh` is a symlink and that no regular file is written for it.

## Out of scope
- `crates/issue-dag-git/tests/git_repository.rs` `a_configured_fsmonitor_is_never_run` writes an executable hook the same way. There, an `ETXTBSY` would hide a run instead of failing a test, so it is a separate concern, tracked separately if wanted.
- The `issue-dag-gh` adapter itself.

## Prerequisites
None.

## Safe intermediate state
Not applicable, because the change lands in one pull request.

## Acceptance
- [x] The Linux reproduction in 2c gives 0 failing runs of 200, where it gave 8.
- [x] The new test fails against the current fake and passes after the fix.
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --locked` and the Python suite pass.

## 1. Background Context
`fake/mod.rs` gives each test a temporary directory with a `bin/gh` it writes (`#!/bin/sh` and `exec python3 .../tests/fake_gh.py`), marks executable, and puts first on `PATH`. The tests run on parallel threads, and each spawns `gh`.

## 2. Observed
PR flyingrobots/taskalisk#121 (CI run 45832908530, job "Rust workspace") failed `a_listing_that_fills_its_limit_is_unavailable_never_a_short_list` with `left: "gh.command_failed"`, `right: "gh.list_limit_reached"`. `main` passed at the same base, bbc46d6.
## 2b. Expected
Every forge test passes on every run.
## 2c. Reproduction
In `rust:1.100.0-bookworm` (Docker, 10 CPUs), build the `forge` test binary once and run it 200 times: 8 runs fail, each in one test, among them `c15_a_run_over_a_strangers_issue_makes_no_edit_history_query`, `a_has_next_page_that_is_missing_or_not_a_boolean_is_refused`, `a_permission_lookup_that_fails_other_than_404_is_unavailable_not_none` and `gh_runs_without_a_terminal_colour_debug_or_prompts`. The messages read `gh could not be run: Text file busy (os error 26)`. macOS: 5 of 5 runs pass.
## 2d. Blast radius
Anyone whose pull request runs the "Rust workspace" CI job: about 4% of runs of that test binary fail (8 of 200, observed in the reproduction). Since `issue-dag-gh` landed in flyingrobots/taskalisk#112. No product code is affected; the adapter is correct.
## 2e. Hypothesis
`ETXTBSY`: a thread forks while another holds the new `bin/gh` open for writing; the child keeps that descriptor until it execs, and any exec of the file meanwhile fails. Killed if the failures persist when no executable is written at test time.
## 2f. Diagnosis
Confirmed by the reproduction's `Text file busy (os error 26)`. Linux refuses to exec a file that any process holds open for writing. `fs::write` holds the descriptor while other test threads fork; the forked child inherits it (`O_CLOEXEC` closes it only at the child's own exec), so an exec of `gh` in that window fails. macOS does not refuse, which is why it passes locally.

## 3. Why now
It fails unrelated pull requests, such as flyingrobots/taskalisk#121.
## 4. Risks
A symlink needs `tests/fake_gh.py` to be executable in every checkout; git records the mode, and the CI checkout keeps it.
## 5. Definition of Done
A regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it, and 0 of 200 failing runs in the reproduction.
## 6. Stakeholders
Every contributor whose pull request runs the Rust CI job.

- flyingrobots/taskalisk#112 added the fake.
- flyingrobots/taskalisk#121 hit the failure.

## Outcome

The executor can launch a coding agent chosen from the user's settings, with a prompt the script builds, under enforced time and process limits.

## Settings

A TOML file in the user's configuration directory (for example `~/.config/taskalisk/settings.toml`), read with the standard library (`tomllib`, Python 3.11+). Agents are listed in order of preference:

```toml
[[agent]]
name = "claude"
argv = ["claude", "-p", "{prompt}"]
timeout_minutes = 90

[[agent]]
name = "codex"
argv = ["codex", "exec", "{prompt}"]
```

The arguments are the user's; the script passes them through. Gate and merge settings live in the same file (flyingrobots/taskalisk#14).

## Scope

- Load and validate the settings; an invalid file fails the run.
- `argv` is a list, never a shell string. Placeholders are a fixed set: `{prompt}`, `{prompt_file}`, `{workdir}`, `{issue}`. An unknown placeholder fails validation.
- Agent selection: the first agent that is installed and passes a probe. Preference order selects at task start; it is not a retry policy, and a failing agent's branch is never handed to the next agent.
- Invocation: a timeout per run that kills the whole process group; a limit on concurrent agents; the prompt file in owned temporary storage.
- Agent commands come only from the user's settings, never from the repository being executed.
- The agent's output never sets task state; callers decide from PR state, CI checks and gate predicates.
- A fake agent command for tests, like `tests/fake_gh.py`.

## Out of scope

- Building task prompts (the task lifecycle, #10) and gate prompts (flyingrobots/taskalisk#14).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Tests over the fake agent cover: selection by preference with an unavailable first agent, placeholder substitution, an unknown placeholder, a timeout that kills child processes, and the concurrency limit.
- [ ] A repository file cannot supply agent commands (test).

## Security requirements (docs/threat-model.md)

- C6: agent `argv` comes from the settings file in the operator's configuration directory, never from the repository being executed; a repository file that supplies a command is ignored and reported.
- C8: the runner refuses to start an agent outside a sandbox (filesystem limited to the worktree and owned temporary storage, network limited to GitHub and the build's registries, scoped token, explicit tool allowlist). A permission-bypass flag is a validation error outside that sandbox.
- C14: the runner passes agents a scoped token from the settings, never the operator's primary `gh` token; minimal environment.
- C16: the prompt file is created with `tempfile.mkstemp` inside a `0700` directory and removed after the run.
- Language decision to record here before implementation: TypeScript (reusing `@git-stunts/plumbing`, `trailer-codec`, `vault`, `alfred`) or Python (`git interpret-trailers`); the compiler stays as it is either way.
- Tests: repository-supplied command rejected; bypass flag outside a sandbox rejected; prompt file mode and cleanup; timeout kills the process group.

## Outcome

A ready-for-review PR passes a user-defined merge gate before it merges, and the frontier rolls forward after the merge.

## Settings

In the settings file from flyingrobots/taskalisk#13, with a global default and per-repository overrides:

```toml
[gate]
predicates = ["pr-review:coderabbitai=APPROVED"]
merge = false   # opt in to merging when the gate passes

[repo."flyingrobots/taskalisk".gate]
predicates = ["cmd:./scripts/acceptance.sh", "skill:baker-street=READY"]
merge = true
```

## Scope

- Predicates, all of which must hold: `pr-review:<login>=<state>`, `cmd:<command exits 0>` and `skill:<name>=<verdict>`. A `skill:` predicate runs an agent through flyingrobots/taskalisk#13 with a prompt from the shared builder and needs a structured verdict; without one, it fails closed.
- Gate commands come only from the user's settings, never from the repository.
- On failure: the PR goes back to draft with a comment giving the verdict, and the agent gets the verdict in its next prompt. A retry budget per run; once it is spent, the task is parked (PR closed unmerged, branch kept, `.status: parked`) and reported.
- On pass: merge only when `merge = true`; otherwise stop at ready-for-review. After a merge, recompile and continue with the new frontier.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Tests for each predicate kind passing and failing, including a `skill:` predicate without a structured verdict (fails closed).
- [ ] A gate failure returns the PR to draft; the retry budget parks the task.
- [ ] With `merge = false` nothing merges; with `merge = true` the merged task's child is selected next.

## Security requirements (docs/threat-model.md)

- C13: gate only PRs that pass C4 (same-repository head, trusted author) and carry the executor's Stage 1 provenance (C10). CI results count only for same-repository heads; a fork PR runs its own workflow file.

## Outcome

A task can declare how much of a shared, finite budget it consumes or frees, for example package bytes. The planner then reports which merge orders of the open tasks fit the budget, and flags any batch that would exceed it.

## Background

On 2026-11-08 in git-stunts/git-warp, the package payload (a 3,300,000-byte unpacked ceiling) became the bottleneck for the whole v21 milestone. Several PRs had already gone red on it before anyone planned around it. The fix depended on order: one task (#1054) freed about 70,875 bytes, and about 44,000 bytes of other PRs could land only after it.

Neither existing resource model fits:
- `.holds` is mutual exclusion, not a budget.
- `.meters` meter simultaneous holders, not cumulative consumption. A merged PR keeps using its bytes for good.

## Proposed shape (to be decided in the PR)

- A frontmatter key such as `.budgets: {package-bytes: +11468}`, signed: negative values free the budget.
- A budget catalog, with a name, a capacity, and the current used value read from a command or a pinned number, recorded in the repository and not in issue bodies.
- **Planner output:**
  - the remaining headroom after each merge in a recommended order;
  - the tasks that cannot fit until a freeing task lands;
  - a soft edge "freeing task before consumer", reported as evidence-backed and never written as a hard `blocked_by`.
- Declared values are estimates, so the report states their basis and the date of the last measurement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A schema for budget declarations and the catalog, with validation errors for unknown budgets.
- [ ] A fixture graph shows a recommended order that fits, and flags an order that does not.
- [ ] Freeing tasks are ranked earlier when they unblock consumers.
- [ ] The trust gate still applies: a declaration from an untrusted author is ignored and reported.

## Out of scope

Measuring the budget itself; each repository supplies the current value.

```python
"""Render a Taskalisk --from-github JSON result as a status-coloured Mermaid flowchart.

Legend: light dashed = done, gray = blocked, green = open and unclaimed,
blue = active (draft pull request), purple = in review.
"""
import json
import re
import sys

d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
nodes = {}
for wave in d["waves"].values():
    for n in wave:
        nodes[n["id"]] = n

def key(ref):
    return "N" + ref.split("#")[1]

def label(n):
    title = n["title"] if len(n["title"]) <= 44 else n["title"][:41] + "..."
    title = re.sub(r'["<>]', "", title)
    return f'#{n["id"].split("#")[1]} {title}'

def cls(n):
    s, ds = n["status"], n["derived_status"]
    if s == "in-review":
        return "review"
    if s in ("wip", "in-progress"):
        return "active"
    if ds == "blocked":
        return "blocked"
    return "open"

out = ["flowchart LR"]
done = set()
for n in nodes.values():
    for p in n.get("completed_parents", []):
        done.add(p)
for ref in sorted(done, key=lambda r: int(r.split("#")[1])):
    out.append(f'  {key(ref)}["#{ref.split("#")[1]} done"]:::done')
for ref, n in sorted(nodes.items(), key=lambda kv: int(kv[0].split("#")[1])):
    out.append(f'  {key(ref)}["{label(n)}"]:::{cls(n)}')
for ref, n in nodes.items():
    for p in n.get("completed_parents", []):
        out.append(f"  {key(p)} -.-> {key(ref)}")
for e in d["edges"]:
    if e["from"] in nodes and e["to"] in nodes:
        out.append(f'  {key(e["from"])} --> {key(e["to"])}')
out += [
    "  classDef done fill:#f6f8fa,stroke:#afb8c1,stroke-dasharray:4 3,color:#57606a",
    "  classDef blocked fill:#d0d7de,stroke:#8c959f,color:#24292f",
    "  classDef open fill:#dafbe1,stroke:#1a7f37,color:#0f2e17",
    "  classDef active fill:#ddf4ff,stroke:#0969da,color:#0a2540",
    "  classDef review fill:#fbefff,stroke:#8250df,color:#2e1065",
]
print("\n".join(out))
```

Colours there are GitHub's light palette and fixed; the real feature should keep them legible in GitHub's dark mode too (Mermaid `classDef` colours are not theme-aware, so pick fills and strokes that read on both, or emit both variants).
